title: Additive monoidal transport of a finite free module
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be preadditive monoidal categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with finite biproducts and tensor additive in each variable. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] and strong monoidal [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $R$ be a ring object (a monoid object, [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]), let $M$ be a left internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $n\geq0$. Use the transported ring $P(R)$ and transported module $P(M)$ of [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. For a ring object $Q$ write $Q^{\oplus n}$ for the biproduct of $n$ copies of its regular module, with the componentwise action; its underlying injections and projections obey $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=\mathrm{id}_{Q^{\oplus n}}$, with empty biproduct $0$.
If $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ is an $R$-module isomorphism, there is a $P(R)$-module isomorphism
$$\alpha:P(R)^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}P(M).$$
Writing $\iota'_i,\pi'_i$ for the biproduct maps in $\mathcal D$, it satisfies
$$\alpha\iota'_i=P(\theta\iota_i),\qquad \pi'_i\alpha^{-1}=P(\pi_i\theta^{-1}).$$
Thus the transported coordinate and basis maps satisfy the same Kronecker and sum-of-projections identities as the original maps. No braiding, commutativity of $R$, or preservation of a commutative structure by $P$ is required.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X

proof.text:
Write $m_Q:Q\otimes Q\to Q$ for multiplication, for $Q=R$ in $\mathcal C$ or $Q=P(R)$ in $\mathcal D$. On the underlying biproduct $B_Q=Q^{\oplus n}$ the componentwise action is
$$a_Q=\sum_i\iota_i m_Q(\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\pi_i),\qquad \pi_i a_Q=m_Q(\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\pi_i).$$
Its unit and associativity equations become those of the regular module after composing with each $\pi_i$; these projections detect equality since $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=1$. This defines the claimed module, including $n=0$, when its underlying object is zero. The second displayed equation says precisely that $\pi_i$ is linear. For inclusions, tensor additivity and the Kronecker identities give
$$\pi_j a_Q(\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\iota_i)=\delta_{ji}m_Q=\pi_j\iota_i m_Q.$$
Projection detection therefore gives $a_Q(\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\iota_i)=\iota_i m_Q$, so $\iota_i$ is linear as well. This is just the defining linearity equation, not an assertion that arbitrary functors preserve biproducts.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X; explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text:
Put $u_i=\theta\iota_i:R\to M$ and $v_i=\pi_i\theta^{-1}:M\to R$. They are $R$-linear: substitute the linearity equations of the two factors into $(gf)a=g(fa)$. The biproduct identities and $\theta^{-1}\theta=1$, $\theta\theta^{-1}=1$ give
$$v_i u_j=\pi_i\theta^{-1}\theta\iota_j=\delta_{ij}\mathrm{id}_R,$$
$$\sum_i u_i v_i=\theta\Bigl(\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i\Bigr)\theta^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_M.$$
Only bilinearity of composition is used in the second calculation.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X; explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text:
Apply the module-transport functor of [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. The action on the transported regular module is $P(m_R)\mu^P_{R,R}$, which is also the multiplication of the transported ring. Hence this module is exactly the regular $P(R)$-module. The same cited statement sends the linear maps $u_i,v_i$ to linear maps
$$b_i=P(u_i):P(R)\to P(M),\qquad c_i=P(v_i):P(M)\to P(R).$$
The strong monoidal structure supplies the lax structure required by that transport; no symmetry comparison is involved.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X; explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text:
An additive functor preserves zero and finite sums because its map on each Hom group is a group homomorphism. Apply $P$ to the identities of step 2 and use functoriality:
$$c_i b_j=P(v_i u_j)=\delta_{ij}\mathrm{id}_{P(R)},$$
$$\sum_i b_i c_i=P\Bigl(\sum_i u_i v_i\Bigr)=\mathrm{id}_{P(M)}.$$
For $i\ne j$ the first equality uses $P(0)=0$, and for $i=j$ it uses preservation of identity. These statements also cover an empty sum.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X; explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text:
Let $B=P(R)^{\oplus n}$ and use its injections $\iota'_i$ and projections $\pi'_i$. Define actual morphisms
$$\alpha=\sum_i b_i\pi'_i:B\to P(M),\qquad \beta=\sum_i\iota'_i c_i:P(M)\to B.$$
Each summand is linear by steps 1 and 3. Finite sums of linear maps are linear directly: if $f_k a_N=a_T(\mathrm{id}_{P(R)}\otimes f_k)$, then
$$\Bigl(\sum_k f_k\Bigr)a_N=\sum_k f_k a_N=\sum_k a_T(\mathrm{id}\otimes f_k)=a_T\Bigl(\mathrm{id}\otimes\sum_k f_k\Bigr).$$
The empty sum is covered by tensor additivity and bilinearity of composition. Thus both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are $P(R)$-module morphisms.

source.place: Third sentence: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the finite free basis isomorphism to X; explicit finite-coordinate argument

proof.text:
Distribute the finite sums and use the Kronecker identities in $B$ and step 4:
$$\alpha\beta=\sum_{i,j}b_i\pi'_i\iota'_j c_j=\sum_i b_i c_i=\mathrm{id}_{P(M)},$$
$$\beta\alpha=\sum_{i,j}\iota'_i c_i b_j\pi'_j=\sum_i\iota'_i\pi'_i=\mathrm{id}_B.$$
Hence $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ as a module morphism. The same one-sum computations give $\alpha\iota'_j=b_j$ and $\pi'_j\beta=c_j$, proving the two prescribed formulas. When $n=0$, step 4 says $\mathrm{id}_{P(M)}=P(0)=0$, and $\mathrm{id}_B=0$ for the empty biproduct; the empty-sum maps above are therefore still mutual inverses. No positive-rank assumption or nonzero-ring assumption was used.

split_report.summary: Expanded finite-free transport into six explicit coordinate steps, using existing module transport and no new nodes. Corrected the ill-typed unbraided commutativity hypothesis by stating the valid monoid-object generality. Checked transported regular actions, both inverse identities, linearity, coordinates and rank zero.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the third sentence of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the pointwise finite free basis to X. This is the finite-free step (2), third proof paragraph, of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients.

The delivery creates no new nodes. I checked it against lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md sentence 3 (main-20261015) and unit sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients clause 2. The statement change is justified: 'commutative ring object' in an unbraided monoidal category is ill-typed (sk-def-sfb-ring-object defines commutativity only when the category is braided), and dropping it strengthens the item without weakening any conclusion. The sole citer, lem-sfb-subfield-flat step 2, supplies exactly the stated hypotheses: strong monoidal, additive, finite biproducts and tensor additive. It uses only the isomorphism F_X≅E_X^n and the coordinate maps, so it stays valid. Step 3 takes from def-sfb-modobj-transport only what its statement says: the transported multiplication and action, and that P of a linear map is linear. Strong monoidal gives the needed lax structure. I checked steps 1, 2 and 4–6 by hand: the componentwise action's unit and associativity laws, linearity of ι_i (which uses id⊗0=0 from tensor additivity), the Kronecker and sum identities after applying P, linearity of finite sums, αβ=id and βα=id, and both coordinate formulas. Rank 0 (P(M) is zero) and rank 1 with P=id also check out. All proof_deps are definitions, so there is no route issue, no tool_uses and no cycle. Grep of dag/nodes and the blueprint for mapMod, finite free and biproduct found no duplicate; lem-sfb-modobj-abelian needs an abelian ambient category. No SGA is cited. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem monoidalFiniteFreeTransport {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C] [MonoidalCategory C] [HasFiniteBiproducts C] [MonoidalPreadditive C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [MonoidalCategory D] [HasFiniteBiproducts D] [MonoidalPreadditive D] (P : C ⥤ D) [P.Additive] [P.Monoidal] (R : C) [MonObj R] (M : Mod C R) (n : ℕ) (θ : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) ≅ M) : ∃ α : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) ≅ (P.mapMod R).obj M, (∀ i : Fin n, (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) i).hom ≫ α.hom.hom = P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, α.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) i).hom = P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom)) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) j).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom) ≫ P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom) = if i = j then 𝟙 (P.obj R) else 0) ∧ (∑ i : Fin n, P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom) ≫ P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom)) = 𝟙 (P.obj M.X)
